nodes.description: Heterozygous deletions (partial or whole-gene) and, less commonly, missense variants in ITPR1 reduce the dose of functional IP3R1, the endoplasmic reticulum inositol 1,4,5-trisphosphate-gated calcium-release channel. In deletion carriers, loss of one ITPR1 copy reduces ITPR1 RNA and protein; because heterozygous loss of the adjacent SUMF1 gene does not cause a movement disorder, ITPR1 haploinsufficiency - not SUMF1 loss - is the causal mechanism.

nodes.description: No SCA15/16-specific interventional trial exists, but rehabilitation is the mainstay of care for degenerative cerebellar ataxia. Meta-analysis of randomized trials in degenerative cerebellar ataxia found that physiotherapy modestly improves ataxia severity as measured by the Scale for the Assessment and Rating of Ataxia (SARA), supporting balance, coordination, and gait training in SCA15/16.

nodes.description: Reduced IP3R1 disproportionately affects cerebellar Purkinje cells, in which IP3R1 is very highly expressed and supports mGluR1-PLC-IP3 calcium signaling, dendritic integration, synaptic plasticity, and firing precision. Aberrant intracellular calcium homeostasis produces Purkinje-cell dysfunction and, over time, degeneration, reducing inhibitory cerebellar cortical output.

nodes.description: No disease-modifying therapy exists for SCA15/16. Management is supportive: genetic counseling, occupational therapy, speech therapy, mobility aids, fall prevention, and individualized symptomatic treatment of tremor and other complications as ataxia progresses.
